top_story.headline: Air Force awards Raytheon $20.7 billion for AMRAAM missiles with no competition
top_story.dek: The attached 2017 justification approves sole-source lots only through Lot 43, but the award covers Lots 41-47.
paragraphs: The Department of the Air Force awarded Raytheon Company $20,699,334,581 for Advanced Medium Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM) Production Lots 41-47, according to an award notice posted October 23. The notice lists a September 25, 2026 award date and cites the "only one responsible source" authority. The effort covers missile production, variants, spares and sustainment support (FA8556-26-C-B001).

The justification attached to a companion notice for the same solicitation number says Raytheon is the only company that can do the work. It says that in 1997, before the government recouped its second-source investment, Raytheon Company and a competing missile maker merged into Raytheon Missile Systems. The Air Force estimates what it would cost to qualify another source, but both the estimate and the contract value in the document are redacted (companion notice, justification).

The attached justification carries a September 13, 2017 date. It is a class justification for "Lot 34 (FY2020) to Lot 43 (FY2029)" and says it approves additional lots "not exceeding Lot 43, FY2029." The award notice title runs through Lot 47. Neither notice says whether a newer justification covers Lots 44-47.
The award notice's own attachments were not read for this edition, so the justification text comes from the companion notice posted the same day.

sections.headline: Marine Corps books 180 Times Square hotel rooms for Army-Navy Week without competition, $754,920
paragraphs: 39 new sole-source justifications today, 23 of them posted under other notice types such as Special Notices and Award Notices. None repeats an earlier edition. Two of the 39 are the Raytheon AMRAAM justification and award, covered in the Top Story, and two bridge extensions are in the Extensions section.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Marine Corps books 180 Westin Times Square rooms for Army-Navy Week without competition
meta: Limited source: only one responsible source
Department of the Navy (Marine Corps Installations National Capital Region)
blocks.text: The Westin Times Square hotel is an unusual vendor for the government, with no federal contract on record under this name in USAspending. The Marine Corps wants 180 rooms for Marines and civilians from December 7 to 13, 2026, at $699 a night (402 single, 648 double and 30 junior-suite room-nights). The justification says a request for information turned up only one hotel near MetLife Stadium that could hold all 180 people, met security needs and was on the GSA and FEMA fire-safe hotel lists. It was posted as a Special Notice.

blocks.title: Homeland Security keeps Noblis on biosurveillance for the White House and National Security Council without competition
meta: Urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: Noblis, Inc., the incumbent, supports the National Biosurveillance Information Center, and the justification says the center could not do its mission without this task order. It states: "Without this contract, biosurveillance reporting would not be provided to the White House, National Security Counsil, and FSLTT partners." The urgency traces to a "statutorily mandated DHS component re-organization." An October 1 addendum corrected the value and changed the cited authority to the fair-opportunity urgency exception.

blocks.title: Army Medical Command gives incumbent Akima a $7.5 million, three-year IT order without competition
meta: Department of the Army (Mission and Installation Contracting Command, Fort Sam Houston)
blocks.text: The order is under a General Services Administration schedule contract, with a base year and two option years. The Army says Akima Data Management, LLC holds the domain controller scripts and expertise needed for the October 31 cutover from one provisioning system to another, and that a new vendor would risk the command's security authorization. The document says award had to happen to avoid a lapse on October 12.

blocks.title: State Department keeps Deloitte on litigation support for embassy construction disputes without competition
meta: Urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: Deloitte Services LP supports the Office of the Legal Adviser in twelve active cases before the Civilian Board of Contract Appeals, the Court of Federal Claims or the Federal Circuit. It also supports certified claims over embassy and consulate construction that may be appealed. Its two current call orders expire November 30, 2026, and the justification says moving the document repositories would jeopardize defense against "hundreds of millions of dollars worth of claims." The new order has a base year and two option years.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs calls its Washington, D.C. hospital kitchen equipment purchase an emergency after failed accreditation findings
meta: Urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The Washington DC VA Medical Center on Irving Street NW needs a pot-and-pan washing room replaced. The statement of work cites the Joint Commission's June 2026 survey, which rated infection-control deficiencies "HIGH Widespread" and found drains backing up and standing water. The statement of work names Aerowerks and T&S Brass models "or equal." It was posted as a Special Notice.

sections.headline: Air Force research lab asks industry for a hypersonic weapon at one-fifth the cost and five times the production rate

blocks.title: Air Force research lab asks for an air-launched hypersonic weapon at one-fifth the cost and five times the production rate
meta: Department of the Air Force (Air Force Research Laboratory)
blocks.text: A call dated October 9 under the PACER broad agency announcement says it will seek "an operationally relevant, air-launched hypersonic weapon for less than 1/5 the cost and greater than 5x the production rate of current systems." Bidders proposing flight tests must build at least two test vehicles and run at least two flight test events. The announcement's "Research Area 10" covers ordnance, including explosive formulations.

sections.headline: Social Security Administration terminates two IT Concepts call orders, de-obligating $29.8 million; Pentagon backlog adds $632.6 million for a nuclear missile program

Defense items below carry signing dates from July 21 to 23, 2026.

blocks.text: Social Security Administration terminates two IT Concepts call orders

The Social Security Administration terminated two call orders with IT Concepts, Inc. for the government's convenience on October 19. One (modification P00011) was for agency-wide non-systems technical support and removed $20,922,096; the other (modification P00008) was for cybersecurity support for the Office of Information Security and removed $8,843,485. Both modifications also finalized settlements (technical support, cybersecurity).
Notable awards and modifications

Northrop Grumman Systems Corp got $632,600,000 more (modification P00065, a funding-only action) for Ground-Based Strategic Deterrent engineering and manufacturing development and early production, signed July 21 by the Department of the Air Force and just made public; Defense Department contract data is released with a 90-day delay (award).
